messages:
mike: Quick RFC follow-up — tiny-allocation runway idea. TL;DR: keep tiny allocations (<8KB) on a short runway in host staging to avoid immediate offload/evict churn. Thoughts?
sara: Sounds promising. What's the tiny threshold you had in mind — 4KB or 8KB? We see lots of ~3–6KB KV blobs in chat workloads.
lee: Concern: if we pin a lot of tiny objects we might fragment GPU heap. Where would the runway live — host pinned pool or a special on-GPU LRU?
mike: Proposal: runway = host-staging reserved ring for tiny allocations. Life window = config `runway_ms` (default 200ms). If an allocation is touched again within the window, promote to persistent GPU slab. Otherwise let it fall back to host free. Pros: reduces PCIe transfer churn for short-lived hot keys. Cons: uses host memory and adds a promotion path.
anil: Can we reuse the slab allocator's coalescing APIs for runway to avoid tiny-object fragmentation on host side? Also we should add a `sparsify` hint for sparse tensor shards from the model loader so we don't blindly promote them.
katie: We should run an A/B: runway off vs runway on w/ {50,200,500}ms. Measure token latency p50/p95, evict rate, and net PCIe throughput. If runway reduces transfers but increases overall memory pressure that's important to know.
sara: What about combining runway with small allocation pooling (thread-local caches)? Pooling reduces alloc churn CPU-side; runway reduces transfers. Might be complementary but let's be explicit.
mike: Agreed — pooling handles malloc/free cost; runway targets transfer cost. We'll keep both. Implementation note: offload code needs to annotate allocations with `is_tiny` and `runway_deadline` metadata.
ops-bot: deploy-bench: experiment/2026-03/runway-proto started on cluster: perf-8xa100-3nodes. Baseline collection started.
lee: Runtime surface: minimal changes — offload path checks `is_tiny` and routes to host-runway rather than immediate evict. Promotion path runs a single-threaded copier to avoid head-of-queue storms.
anil: Corner cases: bursts of pressure — need preemption rules (oldest-first vs LRU across runway). Also when GPU memory is under pressure, runway should be preemptable immediately.
katie: Suggested metrics: `runway_hit_rate`, `runway_promote_rate`, `runway_eviction_rate`, `runway_avg_hold_ms`, and `runway_bytes_in_use` (node-level). Add them to the perf dashboard.
mike: Decision proposal: prototype behind flag `runtime.enable_tiny_runway` default off. Add runway memory cap per node (config `runway_max_bytes`) and preempt policy `runway_preempt=oldest`. Run 2-week benchmark then decide. I'll open a PR with prototype, metric emits, and A/B harness.
sara: +1 to prototype + cap. Also add a safety valve: when host memory crosses `host_staging_high_watermark` we demote runway immediately.
lee: +1. Add unit tests for fragment coalescing and a fuzz test for promotion race.
anil: I'll coordinate with storage/model-loading to add `sparsify` hint so sparse shards don't get promoted unnecessarily.
katie: I'll add the experiment to perf dashboard and tag eng-runtime, eng-ml, and infra.
mike: Thanks all — I'll open PR today and put this on the eng-runtime sync agenda. :tada:
